skill.name: specsfy-aux-stack
skill.description: Inspects project manifests and structural files, then updates .specsfy/STACK.md with detected frameworks, languages, runtimes, testing tools, and persistence technologies.
skill.summary: Maintain an evidence-based project stack inventory while preserving human-authored documentation.
skill.author: promovaweb

content.value_statement: Project stack documentation often becomes incomplete after dependency changes. This skill detects supported technologies and updates .specsfy/STACK.md while preserving human-authored content.
actual_capabilities: Reads composer.json and package.json from a selected project root.
Detects supported PHP, Node.js, framework, testing, and persistence technologies.
Recognizes Laravel, Next.js, Astro, React, Prisma, Drizzle ORM, Pest, PHPUnit, and Vitest.
Detects Docker Compose files as container infrastructure evidence.
Updates a managed section in .specsfy/STACK.md while preserving text outside that section.
Retains existing managed rows and avoids duplicate inventory entries.
limitations: Detection is limited to technologies explicitly listed in the bundled script.
The script does not validate dependency versions or runtime compatibility.
Unrecognized manifests produce an entry that requires manual confirmation.
The skill depends on related Specsfy skills for setup and persistence workflows.

use_cases.title: Refresh stack documentation
use_cases.description: Update the technical inventory after adding or removing major project dependencies.

use_cases.title: Prepare repository context
use_cases.description: Create a concise stack reference before another agent begins implementation work.

use_cases.title: Review technology evidence
use_cases.description: Compare documented stack entries with manifests, lockfiles, and configuration files.

prompt_templates.title: Update the stack inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $specsfy-aux-stack to inspect this project and update .specsfy/STACK.md.

prompt_templates.title: Document a framework change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $specsfy-aux-stack after the recent framework changes. Preserve existing human notes and cite evidence for each new stack entry.
prompt_templates.scenario: Refresh documentation after adding or replacing a framework.

prompt_templates.title: Verify stack documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $specsfy-aux-stack to compare .specsfy/STACK.md with current manifests and configurations. Mark unsupported claims for conversational review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Audit an existing inventory for accuracy.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a persistence update
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $specsfy-aux-stack to refresh the stack inventory after persistence changes. Invoke the related database workflow when required and preserve manual decisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate stack and database documentation after an architecture change.

output_examples.input: Update the stack inventory for a Laravel project using Pest.
output_examples.output: The managed inventory lists PHP, Laravel, and Pest with composer.json as evidence. Existing notes outside the managed section remain unchanged.

output_examples.input: Refresh documentation for a Next.js project using Prisma and Vitest.
output_examples.output: The inventory records Node.js, Next.js, Prisma, and Vitest with package.json evidence, without duplicating existing entries.

output_examples.input: Inspect a repository with no recognized manifests.
output_examples.output: The inventory records that the framework requires confirmation and states that no recognized manifest was found.

best_practices: Confirm the project root before running the update script.
Review each generated row against manifests, lockfiles, and configuration files.
Keep human decisions and notes outside the managed stack block.
anti_patterns: Do not add technologies without evidence from project files.
Do not remove human-authored content outside the managed block.
Do not copy complete dependency trees into the stack inventory.

faq.question: Which files does the skill inspect?
faq.answer: It reads composer.json, package.json, optional Docker Compose files, and the existing .specsfy/STACK.md file.

faq.question: Does it preserve manual documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It replaces only the managed specsfy:stack block and preserves content before and after that block.

faq.question: Which technologies can it detect?
faq.answer: It detects selected PHP, Node.js, framework, testing, persistence, React, TypeScript, and container technologies.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies?
faq.answer: No. It reads manifests and writes stack documentation without installing packages.

faq.question: What happens when no supported manifest is found?
faq.answer: It adds a placeholder stating that the framework requires confirmation.

faq.question: Can it document database changes?
faq.answer: It detects selected persistence packages and directs broader persistence changes to the related database skill.
